name: spread_dynamics_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Bid-ask spread expansion in Indian equities precedes short-term volatility by 1-3 minutes because market makers widen quotes before anticipated information events (pre-news, large order detection). After the volatility event, spreads contract back to normal levels, and prices often overshoot then revert. The strategy: (1) detect spread expansion events (>2x normal), (2) wait for the volatility event to occur (price moves), (3) fade the move when spreads begin contracting (informed participants have completed their activity). The inefficiency persists because: (1) real-time spread monitoring is not standard on Indian retail platforms, (2) the window between spread contraction and price reversion is narrow (1-3 min), and (3) trading during wide-spread periods requires precise limit order placement that is psychologically difficult.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, typical bid-ask spread < 5 bps

conditions: close > low of spread expansion period
close < high of spread expansion period

entry.entry_price: limit order at midprice when spread_ratio < 1.8

exit.target: reversion to pre-event price (50-70% of event move)
exit.stop_loss: event move extends by 50% (e.g., if price dropped 20 bps, stop at -30 bps)
exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing after 10 bps reversion achieved

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L notional, reduce to ₹50K if spread_ratio peaked above 3.0 (high uncertainty event)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, spread expansions are more often informed
filters.time_filter: skip first 10 min and last 10 min (spreads naturally volatile)
filters.volume_filter: volume during spread event > 2x normal (confirms actual event, not illiquidity)
filters.trend_filter: fade only moves that are counter to the day's VWAP trend
filters.spread_filter: only trade when spread_ratio peaked > 2.0 but has started contracting
filters.event_filter: skip if the spread event coincides with scheduled news (informed, no reversion)
other_filters: skip if stock had > 2 spread events already today (repeated events suggest persistent information flow)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — spread dynamics are observable to sophisticated participants but the contrarian entry (fading the event move) is psychologically difficult, keeping retail crowding low.

weaknesses: Spread expansion may indicate a genuine information event (earnings leak, regulatory action) where the price move is permanent, not temporary. Fading such moves leads to large losses.
Limit order entry during spread contraction may not fill — if the reversion starts before fill, the entry is at a worse price; if it doesn't fill, opportunity is missed.
Low signal frequency (3-6 per day across the universe) limits the strategy's contribution to overall portfolio returns.
prior_art: Madhavan (2000) 'Market Microstructure: A Survey' covers spread dynamics theory. Huang & Stoll (1997) 'The Components of the Bid-Ask Spread'. Glosten & Milgrom (1985) foundational model of spread as adverse selection cost. Copeland & Galai (1983).
notes: The critical implementation detail is detecting the spread expansion peak in real-time — you need to identify that the spread has peaked and started contracting, not just that it is wide. This requires a rolling max with lookback. Consider pairing this with the adverse_selection_filter (strategy 107) to avoid informed events.
